evidence.description: Fresh re-read: `const safeObservation = redactPrivateKeyPatterns(skillResult.output || '').slice(0, 1200);` (line 447) and `result: safeObservation.replace(/\s+/g,' ').slice(0, 900)` (line 465). FIND-006's corrected '900-char' / '1200-char intermediate' figures in behavioral-spec.md's Problem section (lines 14-19), R6 (line 143), R9 (line 169), and INV-NO-PROMPT-REGRESSION (lines 190-192) are all now byte-accurate against the live code.

grep -n '180' across both files returns exactly 5 hits, individually re-classified fresh: behavioral-spec.md:16 ('raised from 180 to 900 chars') and :191 ('must never shrink it back toward 180') are intentional historical/cautionary notes, correctly non-hazardous; behavioral-spec.md:38 and :196 ('lines 180-284') are genuine index.mjs line-number citations for the unrelated loop_detect mechanism, verified real (loopDetectStreak/loopDetectSlot block spans exactly lines 180-284); verification-architecture.md:37 is a live test-fixture threshold that is NOT a ground-truth claim but is still stale -- filed separately as FIND-007 under verification_readiness since behavioral-spec.md itself (the actual requirement source-of-truth) now contains zero remaining false 'current cap IS 180' claims.

FIND-001 re-confirmed: `formatRecord({..., kind: 'loop_detect', slot: avoidSlot, ...})` still carries a real slot field. Fresh recount over the live ~/.anicca/state/ledger.jsonl (now 10743 lines, up from 10720 at iteration-1): loop_detect total=1063, with-slot=238 -- identical to iteration-1/2's cited '238/1063 (22%)', unchanged.

FIND-003 re-confirmed: `redactPrivateKeyPatterns` (PRIVKEY_PATTERN = /0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}/g -> '[REDACTED]') is real and exported from env-filter.mjs exactly as the corrected R6 text describes. grep for 'redactPrivateKeyPatterns' across runtime/loop/*.mjs shows it is called only from env-filter.mjs's own definition and from index.mjs (lines 447, 470, 485) -- brain.mjs (thinkProxy/thinkClaudeP/httpPost, the true source of err.message) has zero calls to it. R6's claim that the brain_transport branch needs a NEW redaction call site (not a reuse) remains accurate.

FIND-005 re-confirmed, and the underlying file has since been updated again (2026-07-08, Franklin migrated from ai.anicca.franklin-sol/StartInterval to ai.anicca.franklin-loop/KeepAlive per the file's own header comment) without contradicting the spec's claim: anicca-a3cdd4 (line 96), Franklin (line 97), and claude-p-proxy (line 99) are each still `keepalive` kind reading a runtime/loop/index.mjs-produced ledger.jsonl; claude-p-pm (line 98) is still `interval` kind over earn/polymarket-trade/earner.log, correctly excluded from R1-R8's ground truth. Minor unrelated observation (not filed as a finding, non-hazardous): the spec's own citation 'confirmed at healthcheck-runtime-loop.sh:97,99' omits line 96 (anicca-a3cdd4) from its line-number list even though anicca-a3cdd4 is one of the three named instances; the underlying factual claim about all three instances is nonetheless correct and independently verified against the live file, so this is a citation-completeness nit with no implementation hazard, not a defect worth blocking on.

Freshly recomputed the Problem section's grounding numbers against live data rather than trusting the spec's own citation: non-clean-wake rate (kind not in {wake,narrate,shutdown}) = 22.9% (~/.anicca) and 23.2% (~/.blockrun), matching the spec's '≈ 23% across both live wake ledgers' claim precisely. Per-slot skill_error+skill_missing+skill_timeout rate for earn/sol-trade = 61.4% (~/.anicca) and 70.7% (~/.blockrun), matching the spec's 'individual slots as high as 61-71%' claim precisely. Both grounding claims remain accurate.
Re-confirmed R5's cited precedent: `export const DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC = Number(process.env.BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC) || 20;` -- exact `Number(process.env.X) || N` idiom match.

Re-confirmed the two reused primitives: `formatRecord` is pure `JSON.stringify(fields) + '\n'`; `appendLedgerLine` is the effectful O_APPEND writer this feature's R6/R7 reuse verbatim, exactly as ground-truth text describes.

Fresh review of the full proof table: unrecognized-kind fail-safe (R1), loop_detect-with-matching-slot exclusion (R2), wake_error-interspersed-among-slot-records independence (R3), empty-ledger shape (R4), threshold boundary one-below/at/one-above (R5), missing-ledger + re-run-overwrite (R7), cross-language shared-fixture parity (R8), zero-new-self-fix-callsite static grep (R10) are all still present and internally consistent. No new edge-case gap found distinct from FIND-007 (which is a test-quality/coverage issue on an already-enumerated requirement, not a newly-missed edge case).

The requirement text itself (the source-of-truth an implementer codes against in Phase 2b) is now internally consistent post-FIND-006: no requirement instructs or implies a stale/wrong numeric cap. The one remaining stale-adjacent '180' (FIND-007) lives only in verification-architecture.md's test description, not in any REQ text, so it creates a verification-quality gap, not an implementation-ambiguity hazard of the kind FIND-006 posed in iteration-2.

EARS SHALL-format requirements R1-R10 remain sequential and independently testable; invariants remain explicitly tagged and cross-referenced (INV-NO-JUDGMENT, INV-NO-PROMPT-REGRESSION, INV-LOOPDETECT-SEPARATE, INV-NO-AUTOACTION); Scope IN/OUT and E2E-necessity sections remain complete; purity boundary section and test file layout remain coherent. No structural/format defects introduced by the iteration-2 edits or found on this fresh pass.

The R6 proof-table row's OWN test-fixture threshold ('mock skill exits 1 with >180-char stdout' -> 'detail LONGER than 180 chars') was not among FIND-006's five explicitly-listed correction targets and remains stale relative to the now-corrected 900/4000-char figures elsewhere in the same requirement. As literally worded, a mock fixture anywhere in the 181-900 char range satisfies this assertion while never exercising the boundary where the ledger's result field (900-char cap) would truncate but harness-failures.jsonl's detail field (4000-char cap) would not -- the exact scenario R6 exists to solve per the Problem section's own stated rationale. See FIND-007.
